mainTopic: The שופר on ראש השנה: what may be done to prepare it, whether women and children may blow, and training children even on שבת.
overview: The גמרא goes through several lines of the משנה about the שופר on ראש השנה. First it explains that cutting the שופר is forbidden both with a sickle (a שבות) and with a knife (a לא תעשה), and that the משנה names both in a 'this, and certainly that' style. Next it learns from the משנה that water or wine may be poured into the שופר but urine may not, and says this follows אבא שאול, who forbids urine out of respect for the שופר. Then the משנה says we do not stop children from blowing, which suggests that women are stopped. A ברייתא says women are not stopped either. אביי settles this: the משנה follows רבי יהודה, and the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי ורבי שמעון, who argue in the same way about women doing סמיכה. Finally, רבי אלעזר and a ברייתא teach that we train children to blow even on שבת. The גמרא then points out that this ברייתא seems to contradict itself and begins to answer, an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה: no cutting the שופר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that one may not cut the שופר on ראש השנה, whether the cutting involves a rabbinic prohibition or a Torah prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not cut the שופר, neither with something forbidden because of a rabbinic prohibition nor with something forbidden because of a Torah prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה so it can explain it. This sets up the next step, where the two kinds of cutting are defined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though blowing שופר is a מצוה, preparing the שופר by cutting it is not allowed on the holiday. The משנה lists two levels of prohibition, rabbinic and Torah, without yet saying what each one looks like.

keyTerms.meaning: Cutting, here meaning cutting the שופר to fix or prepare it
A rabbinic prohibition on certain activities on שבת or יום טוב
A Torah-level negative commandment

phrases.english: And one may not cut it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the שופר, which the משנה has been discussing.

phrases.english: neither with something that is forbidden because of a rabbinic prohibition

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין בְּדָבָר שֶׁהוּא מִשּׁוּם לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: nor with something that is forbidden because of a Torah prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion by quoting the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cutting the שופר on ראש השנה is forbidden, at both the rabbinic and the Torah level.

steps.title: Sickle versus knife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that cutting with a sickle is the שבות case and cutting with a knife is the לא תעשה case.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbinic prohibition means a sickle. The Torah prohibition means a knife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a real example for each of the two kinds of cutting in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A knife is the normal tool for cutting, so using it is a full Torah-level מלאכה. A sickle is not the usual tool for this job, and cutting in such an unusual way is only forbidden by the rabbis.

keyTerms.meaning: A sickle
A knife

phrases.english: Because of a rabbinic prohibition: a sickle.
A Torah prohibition: a knife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the two categories named in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cutting with a sickle is a שבות; cutting with a knife is a לא תעשה.

steps.title: Why mention the obvious case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if even a rabbinic prohibition is not set aside for the שופר, it should be obvious that a Torah prohibition is not. Why did the משנה need to say both?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you said even a rabbinic prohibition is not allowed, do you really need to say a Torah prohibition is not allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the משנה, because the second half seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the weaker prohibition, a שבות, is not set aside for the מצוה, then the stronger one, a לא תעשה, certainly isn't. So mentioning the Torah prohibition looks like extra words in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Now', meaning 'now that we already know...'
'Is it even necessary?' This is used when something seems obvious.

phrases.english: Now, if for a rabbinic prohibition you said no,
is it necessary to say so for a Torah prohibition?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the משנה quoted in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's mention of the לא תעשה case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is a קל וחומר: if a שבות is forbidden, a לא תעשה obviously is too, so the extra clause seems pointless.

steps.title: The 'this, and certainly that' style
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is simply teaching in a known style: it states one case, and the other case is understood to be true even more so.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה teaches in the style of 'this, and there is no need to say that.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the extra phrase is just a teaching style, not a new law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה admits the Torah case is obvious and mentions it anyway, in a 'this, and all the more so that' pattern. So the wording does not hint at any hidden extra rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This, and no need to say that': a style where the more obvious case is added anyway
'It teaches'

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for a new law in the words 'לא תעשה' here. The גמרא admits that part is obvious; it is only a style of teaching.

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר זוֹ קָתָנֵי.
phrases.english: It teaches in the style of: this, and there is no need to say that.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר זוֹ קָתָנֵי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the משנה's style of teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra clause seemed to need a special reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is the 'this, and certainly that' style; no extra law is being taught.
steps.whatToRemember: Cutting the שופר is forbidden both with a sickle (a שבות) and with a knife (a לא תעשה). The second case is mentioned only as a 'certainly that' add-on.

steps.title: The משנה: water or wine may be added
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה: one may pour water or wine into the שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he wants to put water or wine into it, he may put it in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה, which allows something. This sets up an inference in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pouring liquid into the שופר is a kind of preparation that is allowed, unlike cutting. It helps the שופר sound clearer.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But', marking a contrast with what was forbidden before
'He may put it in'

phrases.english: But if he wishes to put
water or wine into it, he may put it in.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אִם רָצָה לִיתֵּן לְתוֹכוֹ מַיִם אוֹ יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water or wine may be poured into the שופר on ראש השנה.

steps.title: Inference: urine is not allowed
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה naming only water or wine, the גמרא infers that urine is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Water or wine, yes. Urine, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה closely and pulls out a hidden rule: since only water and wine are listed, urine must be excluded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה could have allowed any liquid but chose to list specific ones. This detail suggests that urine, which also helps the sound, is forbidden. It raises the question of whose view this is.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means 'yes'
Urine

phrases.english: Water or wine, yes;
urine, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַיִם אוֹ יַיִן — אֵין, מֵי רַגְלַיִם — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the clause quoted in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Urine may not be put into the שופר.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the view of the משנה that forbids urine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which Sage the משנה follows, in light of the inference about urine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the inference produced a specific ruling, forbidding urine, the גמרא wants to tie it to a known תנא who holds that view.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
'Who is it?', meaning whose opinion this is

phrases.english: Whose view is our משנה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the inference in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא behind the משנה's ruling that urine is excluded.

steps.title: It is אבא שאול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows אבא שאול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the תנא whose view the משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming אבא שאול tells us the ruling against urine is his position. Proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא

phrases.english: It is אבא שאול.

steps.title: אבא שאול's ברייתא: respect for the שופר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where אבא שאול permits water or wine to clear the sound, but forbids urine out of respect.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: אבא שאול says, water or wine is allowed, to make the sound clear. Urine is forbidden, because of respect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the משנה is אבא שאול by quoting a ברייתא where he gives exactly this ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא שאול agrees that liquids help clear the שופר's sound. Even though urine would also help, putting it into an object used for a מצוה is disrespectful, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As it was taught' in a ברייתא
To make it clear or polished, here meaning a clearer sound
Because of respect, here for the שופר of the מצוה

steps.whatToRemember: Water or wine may be put into the שופר to clear its sound. Urine may not, out of respect for a מצוה object. This is the view of אבא שאול.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that respect for an object used for a מצוה can forbid something that would otherwise help the מצוה.

phrases.english: As it was taught: אבא שאול says:

phrases.aramaic: מַיִם אוֹ יַיִן — מוּתָּר, כְּדֵי לְצַחְצְחוֹ.
phrases.english: Water or wine is permitted, in order to make it clear.
phrases.notes: He means making the שופר's sound clearer.

phrases.english: Urine is forbidden, because of respect.

steps.raayaObject: That the משנה follows אבא שאול
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting אבא שאול forbidding urine because of respect

steps.title: The משנה: we do not stop children from blowing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: we do not stop children from blowing the שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not stop the children from blowing the שופר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה so that it can analyze it. This line sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if children want to blow the שופר on ראש השנה, nobody holds them back. Notice that the משנה only mentions children. The גמרא will build on that detail right away.

keyTerms.meaning: We stop / hold back (someone from doing something)
Children (here, those not yet obligated in מצוות)
To blow (the שופר)

phrases.english: We do not stop the children from blowing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of pouring water or wine into the שופר to the משנה's next line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Children are not stopped from blowing שופר.

steps.title: Inference: women would be stopped
steps.stepSummary: Since the משנה mentions only children, the גמרא infers that women would be stopped from blowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that women are stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה carefully. Because it only says children are allowed, it seems women are not allowed. This sets up a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like children, women are not obligated in שופר. So if the משנה permitted both groups, it could have said so. Since it named only children, the גמרא concludes that women would be stopped.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies / but then (introduces an inference from what the text left out)
Women

phrases.english: This implies that women — we do stop them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from what the משנה left out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By implication, women are stopped from blowing שופר.

steps.title: A ברייתא says women are not stopped either
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that neither women nor children are stopped from blowing on יום טוב, which contradicts the inference.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: we stop neither the women nor the children from blowing on יום טוב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference by quoting a ברייתא that clearly lets women blow too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference from the משנה says women are stopped. The ברייתא says outright that women are not stopped. So the two sources seem to disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a contradicting source)
A festival day (here, ראש השנה)

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: אֵין מְעַכְּבִין לֹא אֶת הַנָּשִׁים
phrases.english: But it was taught: we do not stop the women

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֶת הַתִּינוֹקוֹת מִלִּתְקוֹעַ בְּיוֹם טוֹב!
phrases.english: nor the children from blowing on יום טוב!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference made in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that women are stopped from blowing שופר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly says women are not stopped, which contradicts what we inferred from the משנה.

steps.title: אביי: the two sources follow different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the משנה follows רבי יהודה, and the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי ורבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is not difficult. This one follows רבי יהודה, and that one follows רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction. He says the משנה and the ברייתא simply follow different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no real contradiction, because this is a known מחלוקת. The משנה, which stops women, follows רבי יהודה. The ברייתא, which lets women blow, follows רבי יוסי ורבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: אביי, an אמורא
It is not difficult (introduces an answer)
This one... that one... (assigns each source to a different opinion)

phrases.english: אביי said: It is not difficult:
this one follows רבי יהודה,
phrases.notes: "This one" is our משנה, which stops women.

phrases.english: that one follows רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the two sources to different תנאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the משנה and the ברייתא represent the same view, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, who does not let women do optional מצוות. The ברייתא follows רבי יוסי ורבי שמעון, who allow it.

steps.title: Proof: their מחלוקת about women doing סמיכה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה says only men do סמיכה, while רבי יוסי ורבי שמעון say women may do it if they choose.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: "Speak to the sons of Israel." The sons of Israel lean their hands, but the daughters of Israel do not. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say: Women may lean their hands as an option.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that this מחלוקת exists. It quotes a ברייתא where these תנאים argue about whether women may do סמיכה on a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Women are not obligated in סמיכה, just as they are not obligated in שופר. רבי יהודה does not let them do it, while רבי יוסי ורבי שמעון let them do it if they want. The same split carries over to blowing שופר.

keyTerms.meaning: Lean their hands on a קרבן before it is slaughtered (סמיכה)
Sons of Israel (read here as men only)
Optional: allowed, but not required

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source for the idea that, according to רבי יוסי ורבי שמעון, women may choose to do a מצוה they are not obligated in.

phrases.english: As it was taught: "Speak to the sons of Israel."
The sons of Israel lean their hands,
but the daughters of Israel do not lean their hands,
these are the words of רבי יהודה.
רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say:
Women may lean their hands — as an option.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's answer by showing the מחלוקת exists.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי ורבי שמעון disagree about women doing optional מצוות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about סמיכה on קרבנות, based on ויקרא 1:2.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה (women are stopped) follows רבי יהודה. The ברייתא (women are not stopped) follows רבי יוסי ורבי שמעון, who let women do סמיכה as an option.

steps.title: The משנה: we work with children until they learn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: we work with the children until they learn to blow.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we work with them until they learn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה in order to discuss it. This sets up רבי אלעזר's comment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה goes further than just not stopping children. It says adults actively help and train them until they know how to blow properly.

keyTerms.meaning: We work with / occupy ourselves with (train)
Until they learn

phrases.english: But we work with them until they learn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה after finishing the discussion about women.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We actively train children to blow שופר.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: even on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that we train the children even when ראש השנה falls on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר adds a detail to the משנה: the training of children applies even on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might have thought that on שבת, when the שופר is generally not blown, we would not let children practice. רבי אלעזר teaches that we still train them.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי אלעזר, an אמורא
Even on שבת

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר said: even on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds how far the משנה's rule reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Children are trained to blow שופר even on שבת.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא also says we train children even on שבת, and we certainly do not stop them on שבת or יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught: We work with them until they learn, even on שבת. And we do not stop the children from blowing on שבת, and there is no need to say on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא matches רבי אלעזר: training is allowed even on שבת. It adds that children are not stopped on שבת, and all the more so on a weekday יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports the statement)
There is no need to say (it is obvious)

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:

phrases.aramaic: מִתְעַסְּקִין בָּהֶן עַד שֶׁיִּלְמְדוּ, אֲפִילּוּ בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: We work with them until they learn, even on שבת.
And we do not stop the children from blowing on שבת,
and there is no need to say on יום טוב.
phrases.notes: He means a ראש השנה that falls on a weekday.

steps.raayaObject: That children are trained to blow שופר even on שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same ruling.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The first line of the ברייתא suggests we tell children to blow, but the second line suggests we only don't stop them.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא itself is difficult. You said: We work with them until they learn, even on שבת. This shows that we tell them from the start, "Blow!" Then it teaches: We do not stop them. That means only that we don't stop them, but we do not tell them from the start, "Blow!"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that two lines in the same ברייתא seem to clash. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "We work with them" sounds like active encouragement: we tell them to blow. "We do not stop them" sounds passive: we just let them blow if they want. Both cannot describe the same case.

keyTerms.meaning: This source itself is difficult (it contradicts itself)
This shows that / apparently
From the start, before anything is done
Stopping / holding back

steps.confusionAlert: Training children and not stopping them may sound like the same thing, but they are not. Training means we tell them to blow. Not stopping means we only allow it.

phrases.english: This itself is difficult,
you said: we work with them until they learn,
and even on שבת —
this shows that from the start we say: Blow.
And then it teaches: we do not stop them —
it is only stopping that we do not do,
but from the start we do not say: Blow!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the internal consistency of the ברייתא brought as support.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Its first line implies active encouragement (we tell children to blow), while its second line implies only passive permission (we just don't stop them).

steps.title: The answer begins: the two lines are not really in conflict
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens its answer to the contradiction in the ברייתא by saying 'לא קשיא', and starts pointing to a specific case with 'כאן'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering the contradiction from Step 18 by saying there is no real problem. This line is a setup: the actual explanation comes in the next words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לא קשיא' tells us the גמרא will not drop either line of the ברייתא. Instead, it will show that each line fits a different situation. The word 'כאן' ('here') starts that split, and a matching 'כאן' ('there') will follow for the other line.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, meaning 'in this case'. It is used to point each source or line to its own situation.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop reading at 'כאן'. This word alone is not the answer. It opens a 'כאן... כאן' (here... there) pattern, and the next words tell you which case each line of the ברייתא is about.

phrases.english: This is not difficult. Here,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the קשיא of Step 18 by starting to split the two lines of the ברייתא into separate cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (כאן... כאן): each line of the ברייתא refers to a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two lines of the ברייתא seemed to contradict each other about whether we actively tell children to blow or only don't stop them.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both lines stand. Each one applies to its own case, which the גמרא is about to spell out.
